facts.text: Benton was named for Missouri senator Thomas Hart Benton in 1836, honoring his influence on western expansion.
William P. settled Benton in 1828, establishing the town's early roots and laying the groundwork for its future growth.
In 1829, Benton became the county seat, replacing Beatties Bluff and quickly emerging as the region's administrative hub.
A historic marker on Main Street commemorates Benton’s early history, highlighting its founding and the settlers who shaped the community.
The 1966 March Against Fear civil‑rights march crossed Benton’s streets, bringing national attention to the town during a pivotal era.
Benton Country Club offers a classic golf experience within the town, featuring a well‑maintained course that attracts both locals and visitors.
